newsitem.title: IRAQ: Syrian team discusses in Baghdad border demarcation.
newsitem.headline: Syrian team discusses in Baghdad border demarcation.

text.p: An official Syrian delegation began talks in Baghdad on Wednesday on border demarcation between Iraq and Syria, a Syrian official said.

"We are here within a Syrian-Iraqi border committee," the Syrian official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters. "Every thing is right. There are no differences...It is only technical work to implement a de facto situation."
He said the Syrian delegation included officials from the foreign ministry.
The committee held a first meeting on Wednesday and is expected to meet again over the next two days, he added.
Iraq and Syria decided two months ago to reopen their borders for trade, closed 17 years ago when ties were cut because Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-88 Iraq-Iran war.
Since July the two Arab countries, ruled by rival factions of the Baath party, have been exchanging economic teams.
Direct travel between the two countries, non-existent in recent years, resumed last week when two buses began a daily service between Baghdad and Damascus.

Syrian businessmen want to sell to Iraq goods under the oil pact which allows Iraq oil exports worth $2 billion over six months to satisfy urgent needs of Iraqis hard-hit by U.N. sanctions imposed after the 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The deal, which started in December last year, was renewed for another six months in June.

Iraqi newspapers reported on Wednesday that an Iraqi economic team would travel to Damascus on Friday for talks with Syrian businessmen on supplying Baghdad with humanitarian goods under the oil plan.

Iraq's Trade Minister Mohammed Mehdi Saleh said late last month while opening an exhibition of Syrian medicines in Baghdad that his ministry signed $20 million worth of food contracts with Syria under the oil pact.
The United Nations approved two weeks ago a location on the Iraqi-Syrian border as a new entry point for goods purchased under the pact.
